I have been asked to forward the alert below and ask that patching take place ASAP to minimise the risk. 
 
NHS CYBER ALERT	

 

	CC-4681 - Broadcom Releases Security Updates for VMware ESXi, Workstation, Fusion, and Tools	


Affected Platforms
�	VMware Cloud Foundation
�	VMware vSphere Foundation
�	VMware ESXi
�	VMware Workstation Pro
�	VMware Fusion
�	VMware Tools
�	VMware Telco Cloud Platform
�	VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure
________________________________________
Introduction
Broadcom has released a critical advisory that addresses four security vulnerabilities in multiple VMware platforms, which include Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, ESXi, Workstation Pro, Fusion, Tools, and Telco Cloud.

Three of the vulnerabilities could allow an attacker with local administrative privileges to execute code on the host machine and the other vulnerability could lead to information disclosure.
________________________________________
Vulnerability details

CVE-2025-41236
VMXNET3 integer-overflow vulnerability that could allow code execution
CVSSv3 score: 9.3

CVE-2025-41237
VMCI integer-underflow vulnerability that could allow code execution
CVSSv3 score: 9.3

CVE-2025-41238
PVSCSI heap-overflow vulnerability that could allow code execution
CVSSv3 score: 9.3

CVE-2025-41239
vSockets information-disclosure vulnerability
CVSSv3 score: 7.1

Remediation
Affected organisations are encouraged to review Broadcom's VMware advisory VMSA-2025-0013 and VMSA-2025-0013: Questions & Answers and apply the relevant updates.

short_description: Patient booked in but delay in showing up on Symphony
description:
On the 2nd August a patient booked into the Emergency Department at the Grange University Hospital. The patient booked in using the ipad kiosk with eTriage. According to the document the patient booked into the system at 14:38 however the patient didn't show up on Symphony until 15:23. This was a delay of 1 hour 18 minutes between the patient booking in and the staff aware of the patient. This caused delay to the patient being triage and potential treatment. In this instance the delay did not cause harm to the patient but as we do not understand the reasons behind the delay this is a cause of concern. 

There were no other issues with any other patients during this time and no digital issues encountered. 

The call was logged with eConsult to investigate on the 3rd of August and they have come back with the following: "I have explored this with the technical team and they identified a success message shortly after our delivery of the eTriage (�we got a positive ACK back within 3 seconds of the ORU being sent�). So we believe it is a downstream Symphony issue - please could I ask that you log this with them for investigation?"

Please can you investigate and see if there is anything Symphony end that may have contributed to the delay of the patient showing on the system?

Please see our request regarding an ongoing piece of work we're looking to implement at the Trust for improvement of the wristband printers.

Modulus 10 is a check digit method used to detect errors in identification numbers. In the NHS, it�s being adopted for the CHI number when Modulus 11 options are exhausted. It will only be used for new CHI numbers when Modulus 11 is unavailable, ensuring chi numbers can be registered/accepted in our Digital Systems.

�	Current Validation Logic

�	Implementation Timeline
If changes are needed, what is the estimated timeline for delivery and deployment?

short_description: Integration Flags issue for new Patientrack Process
description:
Trust identified an issue when retrospective obs are recorded on patientrack and received via integration (this is a new functionality the Trust have in Production and are looking to progress in to live in February 2026)

When these are recorded retrospectively in patient track they are shown in Symphony in a different order and not in chronological order, symphony integration fail to recognize the NEWS score is a retrospective score and change the score in the symphony tracking grid.

Example.
- Last set of obs is done at 11.00 NEWS=5
- staff record retrospective obs that were done at 10.00 with NEWS=0
- the NEWS in the Symphony tracking grid should remain 5 (as last set of observation) , instead the NEWS score changed to 'zero'.

this introduces a clinical risk:
- discrepancy on what symphony tracking grid and patientrack chart/screens is displaying ( patientrack is the single source of truth)
- risk of staff only looking at symphony and not double checking in patientrack , hence clinical decision/escalation might be missed or based on 'old' score. 

integration issue- symphony , potential high use of retrospective obs functionality  for highly acute patients (esp in RESUS) 

at the moment no existing control ( only education and comms)

Our Trust backup system reported the following error this morning,  due to a local job to backup the SQL log being enabled yesterday for the referenced Symphony database.
Failed backup of the transaction log for SQL Server database 'EMIS_EIE_SouthTees_Upgrade' from 'STAS822\STAS820\MSSQLSERVER'.
Apr 29, 2026, 1:53:47 PM
Error code
RBK20200004
What happened?
The transaction log chain is broken for database STAS822\EMIS_EIE_SouthTees_Upgrade.
Possible cause
The last transaction log backup, '<unnamed log backup>', was performed outside of a Rubrik CDM instance (Last log backup user: 'XSTEES\SASymphony').
Possible solution
Check with the SQL Server administrator to confirm whether any log backup operations are performed outside of a Rubrik CDM instance. If so, start a new log chain by taking an On-demand snapshot for this database.
In SQL Server, each log backup captures only the transactions that have occurred since the immediately preceding log backup. If two systems (e.g., SQL Agent and a third-party backup system like Rubrik) are both taking log backups it fragments the log chain, making data recovery extremely difficult and unreliable.

Hi team, 

Following recent guidance from NHSE, EEMAC is a new NHS England model of care allowing Emergency Medicine teams to manage selected patients beyond the traditional 4 hour standard within an ambulatory setting, while remaining under Emergency Medicine clinical responsibility.

National guidance is explicit that EEMAC is not an admission and remains part of the ED pathway, but that the 4 hour Emergency Care Standard (ECS) clock should stop at the point of transfer into EEMAC, while overall time under Emergency Medicine oversight must still be tracked to ensure patients do not remain in EEMAC in excess of 8 hours. For now the attendance type will remain the same, but in the future it is likely that EEMAC will be type 5 activity recording.

https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/extended-emergency-medicine-ambulatory-care-eemac-operating-principles/

At present we have no current workflow in Symphony that supports EEMAC reporting

We have two options proposed which will support the Trust in capturing this data and a third option that we are hoping you could provide knowledge and insight on. 

Option 1 � is it possible within the existing SJUH/LGI department builds within symphony, to create an EEMAC care group, which would stop the 4hr ECS clock, i.e. if the patient was moved at 2hrs, the patient would show as being seen, treated and discharged within 4hrs, and therefore not a breach, but the overall time in dept. clock would continue to count so that we can ensure the patient doesn�t spend longer than 12hrs on EEMAC.

Option 2 � build a new department for EEMAC, for LGI and SJUH, with type 5 activity reporting and ECDS reporting

Option 3 � Optum / EMIS guidance - Have you created EEMAC requirements for any other sites following this guidance. If so, how was this achieved it? Are you able to share what has worked well in other Trusts?

Functional Requirement 

� Ability to record transfer from ED to EEMAC as a discrete, time stamped event.
� Automatic stop of the 4 hour ECS clock at the point of EEMAC transfer.
� Continued tracking of total Emergency Medicine time, including:
o Time in ED
o Time in EEMAC
� Automated alerts/escalation when:
o Time in EEMAC approaches 8 hours
� Maintenance of continuous ECDS data capture, including:
o Tests, investigations, procedures
o Diagnoses and outcomes
� Recording of EEMAC location / care area for reporting and audit.
Data & Reporting Requirements
� Differentiation between:
o Standard ED attendances
o ED ? EEMAC pathway patients
� Ability to report:
o Volume of EEMAC activity
o Time spent in EEMAC
o Outcomes (discharge, admission, transfer back to ED)
� Alignment with ECDS, without breaking current SUS submissions.

Any guidance on workstreams undertaken by other Trusts would be incredibly useful.

It may be beneficial to set up a meeting to discuss this in further detail. 

Many thanks 

Megan Gregory
